American Public Schools Use KONAMI's Game for Physical Education Programs - Dance Dance Revolution -

Updated on January 1, 2010

KONAMI music game "DanceDanceRevolution" (DDR) has been used in the physical education and health-related curriculums at elementary, junior high and high schools in the U.S. state of West Virginia since January 2006, as a tool for combating the problem of childhood obesity.

DDR encourages children to engage in fitness and fun by dancing to choreographed steps through beginner-friendly and interactive gameplay. Playing the game has provided children with an alternative means to exercise, which is a key factor in improving and maintaining a healthier lifestyle.

Additionally, studies have shown DDR, when used over long periods, also improves overall health and can reduce the risk of diabetes.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 32 Pro Gamers Take the Stage in Rhythm Game Esports Tournament
BEMANI PRO LEAGUE -SEASON 2- beatmania IIDX!

June 1, 2022 15:00

Konami Amusement Co., Ltd.

Konami Amusement Co., Ltd. is thrilled to announce 32 pro gamers have signed contracts to participate in the rhythm game esports tournament BEMANI PRO LEAGUE -SEASON 2- beatmania IIDX. The competition's eight team companies* selected 18 players at the draft held on Friday, April 8. Joining these players are 14 returning players from last season, for a combined total of 32 players, four to a team.

The BEMANI PRO LEAGUE, a new form of entertainment that fuses esports and music, was first held in 2021. In its second season this year, competition will take place across three titles. In addition to last season's "beatmania IIDX," players will also battle it out in "Dance Dance Revolution" and "SOUND VOLTEX." The opening match of the Regular Season for BEMANI PRO LEAGUE -SEASON 2- beatmania IIDX begins Wednesday, June 29 at 9 p.m., and will be livestreamed on the BEMANI PRO LEAGUE official YouTube channel.

With eight companies now participating this year, the competition has switched to a finals tournament format. In the Regular Stage, the eight teams will play a total of 28 matches in a round robin. The top six teams will then advance to the Quarter-Finals, where the bottom four of those teams will split into pairs and play one match against each other. The two winners will progress to the Semi-Finals, where they will face off against the top two teams from the Regular Stage. The two winners of this stage will then meet in the Final.

Tournament Format

Today, Wednesday, June 1, we also posted on the competition's website the complete livestream schedule for the Regular Stage of BEMANI PRO LEAGUE -SEASON 2- beatmania IIDX.

What is BEMANI?

BEMANI is the unified brand name for Konami Amusement's music games. The name comes from an abbreviation of beatmania, which was introduced in 1997, and it is used to refer to Konami Amusement's entire music game lineup.

What is BEMANI PRO LEAGUE?

BEMANI PRO LEAGUE is a new form of entertainment that fuses esports and music, brought to you by KONAMI. Each team will be comprised of professional players who will battle it out for overall victory for their team in league-style battles. In BEMANI PRO LEAGUE -SEASON 2-, the competition titles will consist of "beatmania IIDX," "SOUND VOLTEX" and "Dance Dance Revolution".

What is the beatmania IIDX series?

The beatmania IIDX games are a flagship BEMANI series that was introduced in 1999. In these DJ simulation games, players must press seven keys and spin a turntable to the beat. With their diverse track lists and deep gameplay, they offer an authentic disc jockey experience, and have garnered praise for over two decades.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Culture and Academic

KONAMI titles put on display at "Manga * Anime * Games from Japan" (organized by The National Art Center, Tokyo)

A number of KONAMI game titles, including "Winning Eleven," "JIKKYOU PAWAFURU PUROYAKYU," "METAL GEAR SOLID," and "beatmania," were chosen for the "Manga * Anime * Games from Japan" exhibition organized by The National Art Center, Tokyo. The games were displayed to a great number of visitors.

With a focus on the period from 1989 to the present, the "Manga * Anime * Games from Japan" exhibition presented a comprehensive survey of Japanese manga, anime, and games which have evolved into an integrated form of media expression. The exhibition's aim was to provide viewers with an opportunity to rediscover their imagination and creativity. The exhibition was also held at Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art (from September 19 to November 23, 2015).

List of Titles Exhibited:

  1. "Winning Eleven"
  2. "JIKKYOU PAWAFURU PUROYAKYU"
  3. "METAL GEAR SOLID"
  4. "Tokimeki Memorial"
  5. "LOVEPLUS"
  6. "beatmania"
  7. "Dance Dance Revolution"
  8. "Dance Evolution"
  9. "pop'n music"
